visual_action: A slideshow of still photos of Donald Trump. The first shows him at a podium with an American flag backdrop, looking concerned. The second shows him with a wide-eyed, smiling expression. The third shows him shouting with his hand near his mouth. The final photo is a close-up of him speaking into a microphone. Text overlays appear on each image.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: He is visually present in every photo of the slideshow and is named in the on-screen text, which asks 'How bad is Donald Trump?' and attributes a quote to him.

on_screen_text.text: How bad could Donald Trump possibly be?
“I was able to kill Roe v. Wade... Without me there would be no 6 [week bans].”

spoken_summary: The audio consists of lyrics from a song, which asks, "How bad can I be? I'm just doing what comes naturally. How bad can I be? How bad could I possibly be? Let's see."
audio_music: The audio features the song "How Bad Can I Be?" from the movie "The Lorax." It is an upbeat, theatrical song sung by the film's villain, used here to create a satirical and mocking tone.
editing_pacing: A fast-paced slideshow of still images, with cuts timed to the beats of the background music.
cultural_references: The song "How Bad Can I Be?" from the 2012 animated movie "The Lorax"
Ed Helms (as the singer of the song)
The character The Once-ler (the villain who sings the song in the film)
central_claim: Donald Trump is a villain who proudly takes credit for overturning Roe v. Wade and enabling state-level abortion bans.
intended_effect: To frame Donald Trump as a villain and encourage negative sentiment towards him by associating him with a cartoon antagonist and highlighting his role in overturning abortion rights.
